package_info.why_malicious: This report does not analyze a specific malicious package, but rather discusses systemic risks and attack scenarios in CI/CD pipelines that can lead to software supply chain attacks. The focus is on the risk of malicious code or dependencies being introduced into software via compromised CI/CD infrastructure, credentials, or third-party components.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious code or dependencies are added to source code or build scripts, either directly or via compromised third-party libraries.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During CI/CD pipeline execution, the code executes unauthorized actions such as exfiltrating secrets, modifying build artifacts, or introducing backdoors, resulting in compromised software being deployed to production.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Any code or dependency added without proper review or from untrusted sources can introduce malicious functionality, such as credential theft or backdoors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal CI/CD pipelines should only execute reviewed and trusted code; introducing unreviewed or untrusted code violates this expectation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated dependency updates or build scripts are legitimate if sourced from trusted, verified sources and reviewed.
key_indicators: Addition of new dependencies from untrusted sources
Modifications to build scripts or configuration files without proper review
Code that accesses secrets or environment variables and sends data externally

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious code is appended to standard libraries (e.g., d3dcompiler, ffmpeg) or binaries, which is then executed when the application runs.
malicious_snippets.code_language: binary (compiled code, e.g., C/C++), or injected scripts
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the modified library or binary executes hidden malicious payloads, such as establishing a backdoor or exfiltrating data, resulting in compromise of end-user systems.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Standard libraries or binaries should not contain appended or hidden code; such modifications are a hallmark of supply chain attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate libraries and binaries are expected to match their official, reproducible builds; any deviation is suspicious.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Custom builds for internal use may modify binaries, but such changes should be documented and reviewed.
key_indicators: Unexpected changes to standard libraries or binaries
Presence of appended code or unexplained sections in compiled files

attack_chain.action: Attacker obtains credentials or access to CI/CD infrastructure or source code repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to modify code, configuration, or dependencies.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code or dependencies are introduced into the source code, build scripts, or third-party libraries.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in the build process.

attack_chain.action: CI/CD pipeline builds and signs the compromised software, which may include modified binaries or libraries.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromised software is deployed to production or distributed to end users.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes on end-user systems, exfiltrating data or establishing persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: compromise of end-user environments and data exfiltration.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests during CI/CD builds or from deployed applications
Access to secrets, tokens, or environment variables in build scripts or application code
Modifications to standard libraries or binaries not matching official releases
Addition of new dependencies or code from untrusted sources
file_indicators: Changes to CI/CD configuration files (e.g., .github/workflows/*.yml, Jenkinsfile, etc.)
Unexpected modifications to standard libraries (e.g., d3dcompiler, ffmpeg)
Presence of undocumented or unexplained files in build artifacts
network_indicators: Outbound connections to unknown or suspicious domains during build or runtime
Exfiltration of secrets to external endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor CI/CD pipelines for unauthorized changes to code, configuration, or dependencies. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unexpected modifications to standard libraries or binaries. Analyze network traffic for suspicious outbound connections during builds and from deployed applications. Correlate SBOM data with known vulnerabilities and verify the integrity of all third-party components. Implement reproducible builds and post-compilation integrity checks to ensure no malicious code is present in final artifacts.
